title: Wheat Cultivation Best Practices - Punjab
content: Wheat cultivation in Punjab: Optimal sowing time: Nov 1-25 (irrigated), Oct 15-Nov 10 (barani). Seed rate: 50kg/acre (irrigated), 40kg/acre (barani). Row spacing: 22.5cm (drill sowing). Land preparation: 2-3 plowings + planking. Fertilizer: 1 bag DAP (50kg) + 1 bag urea (50kg) at sowing; 1 bag urea at first irrigation (CRI stage, 20-25 days). Total NPK: 120-60-40 kg/ha. Irrigation: 4-5 irrigations (CRI, tillering, jointing, booting, grain filling). Weed control: Isoproturon (Arelon 50WP, 1kg/acre) pre-emergence or Clodinafop (Topic 15WP, 40g/acre) + Metsulfuron post-emergence. Harvest when grain moisture is 12-14%. Recommended varieties: Faisalabad-085, Lasani-085, Galaxy-13, AAS-11.

title: Rice Basmati Cultivation Guide
content: Basmati rice cultivation: Nursery sowing: June 15-30. Transplanting: July 10-Aug 5 (25-30 day old seedlings). Seed rate: 8-10kg/acre for nursery. Spacing: 20x15cm (2-3 seedlings/hill). Land preparation: Puddling (wet tillage) to create impervious layer. Water management: 2-5cm standing water throughout; drain 15 days before harvest. Fertilizer: 25kg DAP + 25kg SOP at transplanting; 25kg urea at 20 days + 25kg urea at 40 days. Total: 100-50-50 kg NPK/ha. Weed control: Butachlor (Machete 50EC, 1.2L/acre) pre-emergence (3 days after transplanting); Bispyribac-sodium (Nominee Gold 10SC, 100ml/acre) post-emergence at 15-20 days. Stem borer management: Cartap hydrochloride (Padan 4G, 10kg/acre) in whorl at 30 and 45 days. Harvest when 80% grains are straw-colored. Thresh at 14% moisture. Varieties: Super Basmati, PK-386, KS-282.

title: Cotton Cultivation - Sindh and Punjab
content: Cotton cultivation: Sowing time: April 15-May 31 (Sindh), May 1-June 15 (Punjab). Seed rate: 8-10kg/acre. Row spacing: 75cm (rows) x 15-25cm (plants). Land preparation: Deep plowing (30cm) + 2 harrowings + ridging. Fertilizer: 1 bag DAP at sowing; 1 bag SOP at flowering; 1-2 bags urea in 2-3 splits (30, 45, 60 days). Total: 150-50-50 kg NPK/ha. Irrigation: First at 35-40 days, then every 15-20 days. Avoid water stress during flowering and boll formation. Weed control: Pendimethalin (Stomp 330E, 1.2L/acre) pre-emergence; Quizalofop (Targa Super 5EC, 500ml/acre) post-emergence for grasses. Pest management: Pheromone traps for bollworm monitoring; threshold-based spraying. Picking: 3-4 pickings at 7-10 day intervals when 60% bolls are open. Varieties: BT-121, BT-123, MNH-1016, FH-2132 (Bt cotton).

title: Sugarcane Cultivation Practices
content: Sugarcane cultivation: Planting time: September-November (autumn plant), February-March (spring plant). Seed rate: 30-40 double-budded setts/acre (8-10 tons cane/acre). Row spacing: 90-100cm (furrows, 15-20cm deep). Land preparation: Deep plowing (40cm), 2-3 harrowings, leveling. Fertilizer: 3 bags DAP + 1 bag SOP + 1 bag zinc sulfate at planting; 2 bags urea at 45 days + 2 bags urea at 90 days + 1 bag urea at 120 days. Total: 250-100-100 kg NPK/ha. Irrigation: Every 10-12 days (summer), 20-25 days (winter). Earthing up at 90-120 days (partial then complete). Propping with rope/trash to prevent lodging. Trash mulching conserves moisture. Ratoon management: Stubble shaving, gap filling with setts, extra fertilizer (25% more N). Harvest at 12-14 months (plant crop), 10-12 months (ratoon). Brix >18% at harvest. Varieties: HSF-240, CPF-246, S-2003-US-633, L-118.

title: Drip Irrigation for Vegetables
document_title: Drip Irrigation for Smallholder Vegetable Farmers
content: Drip irrigation advantages for vegetables: Water savings: 30-50% compared to furrow irrigation. Fertilizer use efficiency: 40-60% improvement through fertigation. Yield increase: 20-40% with better quality. Reduced disease: Less leaf wetness reduces fungal diseases. System components: Water source, pump, filter (screen+disc), main pipe (PVC 50-75mm), sub-main (PVC 40mm), lateral drip lines (16mm with inline drippers 2-4L/hr at 30cm spacing). Layout: One lateral per row or one lateral for two rows (paired rows). Operation: Daily irrigation (1-3 hours depending on crop stage and weather). Pressure: 1.0-1.5 bar at lateral inlet. Maintenance: Weekly flushing of laterals, monthly filter cleaning, acid treatment (phosphoric acid 0.5%) quarterly to dissolve mineral deposits. Fertigation: Soluble fertilizers (calcium nitrate, potassium nitrate, MAP) injected through venturi or dosatron. EC of irrigation water should be <1.5 dS/m for most vegetables.

title: Soil Health and Organic Matter Management
document_title: Soil Fertility Management for Sustainable Agriculture
content: Pakistan's soils are generally alkaline (pH 7.5-8.5) with low organic matter (<1%). Organic matter improvement: Farmyard manure (FYM): 10-15 tons/acre annually. Green manuring: Grow Sesbania (dhaincha) or Sunnhemp for 45-60 days then incorporate. Crop residue incorporation: 2-3 tons/acre. Compost application: 5-8 tons/acre. Benefits: Each 1% increase in organic matter = 20kg/acre additional N availability, improved water holding capacity (+10%), better soil structure. Soil testing: Before each cropping season. Key parameters: pH, EC, organic matter, available N-P-K, micronutrients (Zn, B, Fe). Gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O): 1-2 tons/acre for sodic soil reclamation (exchangeable sodium >15%). Sulfur: 20-30kg/acre for pH reduction in calcareous soils. Zinc sulfate: 10-15kg/acre for zinc-deficient soils (DTPA-Zn <0.6 ppm). Biofertilizers: Rhizobium for legumes (seed inoculation), Azotobacter for cereals (soil application 5kg/acre).

title: Integrated Pest Management Principles
document_title: IPM Guidelines for South Asian Agriculture
content: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) principles: 1. Prevention: Use resistant varieties, healthy seeds, balanced nutrition, proper irrigation, field sanitation. 2. Monitoring: Regular field scouting (weekly), pheromone traps, sticky traps, economic thresholds. 3. Decision making: Spray only when pest population exceeds economic threshold level (ETL). 4. Biological control: Conserve natural enemies (ladybirds, trichogramma, chrysoperla), avoid broad-spectrum insecticides, release biocontrol agents. 5. Cultural practices: Crop rotation, trap crops, intercropping, timely sowing, destruction of crop residues. 6. Mechanical control: Hand-picking, light traps, bird perches, yellow/blue sticky traps. 7. Chemical control: Last resort, use selective/targeted pesticides, rotate mode of action groups (IRAC classification), follow pre-harvest intervals (PHI), avoid calendar-based spraying. Pesticide safety: PPE (gloves, mask, boots), re-entry interval (REI), proper disposal of containers (triple rinse), never spray against wind.

title: Mango Orchard Management
content: Mango orchard management: Planting: July-August (monsoon). Spacing: 10x10m (traditional), 5x5m (high density). Grafted plants only (1-2 year old). Varieties: Sindhri (main commercial), Chaunsa, Anwar Ratol, S.B. Chaunsa, White Chaunsa. Fertilizer (bearing tree): 500g N + 250g P2O5 + 500g K2O per tree/year, split into 2 doses (pre-flowering Feb + post-harvest Aug). 20-30kg FYM per tree. Micronutrients: Zinc sulfate 200g + Borax 100g per tree annually. Irrigation: Every 10-15 days (summer), 25-30 days (winter). Stop irrigation 2-3 weeks before harvest to improve fruit quality. Flowering management: Paclobutrazol (Cultar 2.3SC, 5ml/m canopy diameter) soil drench in September for early, uniform flowering. KNO3 (1%) spray at flower bud differentiation. Fruit fly management: Methyl eugenol traps (10/acre), protein bait traps, bagging of fruits. Harvest at physiological maturity (shoulder development, color break). Post-harvest: Hot water treatment (52°C, 5min) for anthracnose control.

title: Citrus (Kinnow) Orchard Management
content: Kinnow orchard management: Planting: February-March or July-August. Spacing: 6x6m. Budded plants on rough lemon or citrange rootstock. Fertilizer (bearing tree 8+ years): 800g N + 400g P2O5 + 600g K2O per tree, split into 3 doses (Feb, May, Sep). 40kg FYM per tree. Micronutrients: Zinc sulfate 300g + Ferrous sulfate 200g + Borax 100g per tree (March). Irrigation: Every 7-10 days (summer), 15-20 days (winter). Avoid water stress during fruit set (March-April) and fruit development (June-September). Basin irrigation preferred. Pruning: Remove water suckers, dead/diseased branches, criss-cross branches. Open center canopy for sunlight penetration. Fruit drop management: 2,4-D (20ppm) spray at fruit set (pea size) and again at marble size. GA3 (20ppm) at flowering for better fruit set. Zinc deficiency: Zinc sulfate 0.5% + urea 1% foliar spray (2-3 times). Harvest: December-January (when TSS:acid ratio reaches 12:1). Clip, don't pull fruits.

title: Climate-Smart Agriculture Practices
content: Climate-smart agriculture for Pakistan: 1. Conservation agriculture: Zero/reduced tillage, permanent soil cover, crop rotation. Benefits: 15-20% fuel savings, improved soil moisture retention, reduced erosion. 2. Water management: Laser land leveling (20-30% water saving), alternate wetting and drying (AWD) in rice (30% water saving without yield loss), rainwater harvesting. 3. Heat stress management: Adjust sowing dates (earlier wheat sowing by 10-15 days), heat-tolerant varieties, mulching (rice straw 4-6 tons/acre), evaporative cooling (mist sprinklers). 4. Carbon sequestration: Agroforestry (Eucalyptus, Poplar on field boundaries), green manuring, biochar application (2-5 tons/acre). 5. Early warning: Monitor Pakistan Meteorological Department advisories, use crop growth stage-specific weather forecasts. 6. Crop diversification: Include pulses (mung, mash) in rotation to improve soil health and spread climate risk. 7. Insurance: Crop loan insurance through Zarai Taraqiati Bank (ZTBL) provides coverage against natural disasters.
